validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Every claim checked against the source at a named line; the objection that sank the last plan was verified as correct rather than argued with (trigger renders the `value` prop, onSave/Apply is the only write-back). validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #74 collects eight leftovers from PR #68 (for #61): seven non-blocking review findings plus one QA finding. Seven of the eight are test and test-helper work; one is a product defect.

The seven review findings are one thing seen from seven sides — a hole in the coverage of #61's fix. Hiding Skip on an exhausted recurrence shipped with a test that cannot fail without it: the reviewer reverted all four scheduleIsSkippable call sites to scheduleIsRecurring and `playwright test schedules.test.ts -g "hides skip"` still passed (1 passed, 23.4s). Neither e2e fixture is the discriminating input. The one-off fixture's date condition is a plain date, so scheduleIsRecurring was already false for it (that was #59's fix); the recurring fixture is a plain never-ending monthly, for which getNextDateAfter returns a date under both predicates. The only input where the two disagree is a recurrence whose endMode is after_n_occurrences and whose count is already reached. Around that hole the review found ~50 lines of test that assert a regex still matches literals declared beside it, a console assertion covering only the add path, three method names that describe half their contract, and one fixture hoisted out of the describe block that owned it.

The QA finding is separate and pre-existing. SchedulesTable.tsx:225 puts onClick={() => onSelect(schedule.id)} on the whole row body, Schedules/index.tsx:28-35 wires onSelect={onEdit}, and onEdit dispatches pushModal. pushModal (modalsSlice.ts:755) appends unconditionally — it special-cases only 'keyboard-shortcuts' — while replaceModal (:769) sets modalStack = [modal]. So the second click of a double-click pushes a second identical schedule-edit onto the stack. Modals.tsx:268 renders one ScheduleEditModal per stack entry, so two live copies mount and one Cancel pops only one.

No decision from a person is outstanding: plan/brief.md records none, and the repo already ships both halves of the fix (the two predicates, and a replaceModal reducer for exactly this stacking problem).

ON THE PRE/POST-APPLY SPLIT, which the last review rejected the plan over. I verified the objection against the source and it is correct. RecurringSchedulePicker.tsx:632 renders `{value ? recurringDescription : t('No recurring date')}`, where recurringDescription is memoised on [locale, value, dateFormat] (:612-615). `value` is fields.date (ScheduleEditForm.tsx:261) and is updated only through the picker's onChange, which is called from exactly one place — onSave (:607-609), wired to Apply at :579. Everything before Apply is local to the tooltip: updateField/change-field mutate the tooltip's own reducer (:405-407), the re-seed effect reads the same unchanged currentConfig (:396-401), and the get-upcoming-dates preview only sets previewDates (:410-421). So while the popover is open the trigger still renders the PRE-change value. This plan therefore asserts the 'once' description AFTER Apply, and, separately, asserts the pre-Apply state as its own case: the trigger still reads 'Every month on the 4th' with no ', once' suffix while the popover is open. The singular 'occurrence' label at :461 is a different control, rendered only while the popover is open, and is not what the trigger ever shows.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Two independent causes. (1) Coverage, not code: the e2e fixtures are not the input where scheduleIsSkippable and scheduleIsRecurring disagree, and the unit tests call the predicate directly so they pass whatever the call sites do. (2) Stack discipline: the row's onSelect is a modal opener and uses the appending reducer (pushModal) where the replacing one (replaceModal) belongs; onEdit is the only schedule-edit push on the page, so the two were indistinguishable until a user clicked twice.
validated_work_order.approach: Seven edits in dependency order. (1) Add data-testid="recurrence-description" to the picker's trigger Button (RecurringSchedulePicker.tsx:627-633) — the only handle a test has on the end-mode popover. (2) Add setRecurrenceEndAfterOccurrences(occurrences?) to the schedule-edit-modal page model: open the trigger by testid, pick 'for' in #repeat_end_dropdown, and assert #end_occurrences reads '1' rather than typing into it, because the field is uncontrolled and typing would deliver the string '1' that the popover's singular label accidentally depends on. It does not click Apply — the caller applies, because the post-Apply trigger assertion is the caller's. (3) Extend the 'hides skip' e2e test with a third schedule built through the UI: Repeats, end mode 'for' occurrences 1, Apply, Add — seeded to start today, so it is Due and exhausted, which is the only discriminating input. Assert its menu is ['Post transaction', 'Post transaction today', 'Complete', 'Delete'] with no Skip, while the never-ending monthly keeps Skip; locate rows by payee, not index. Restart is excluded from the contrast (SchedulesTable.tsx:196 hides it for every non-completed row). (3a) Two trigger-text assertions, in order, for a stated reason: BEFORE Apply the trigger still reads 'Every month on the 4th' with no ', once' (pins the write-back boundary); AFTER Apply it reads 'Every month on the 4th, once'. The second cannot be asserted before Apply — the trigger renders the `value` prop and Apply is the only write-back. Never assert 'occurrence' on the trigger; that label is the popover's own. (4) Delete REACT_INPUT_WARNING_PROBES, the alternatives loop and the trailing page.evaluate; keep reactInputWarning, CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS, watchReactInputWarnings, the drain and the assertion — that guard is load-bearing. (5) Drive the edit path inside the watched window so the `fields.name ?? null` seed at useScheduleEdit.ts:119 is exercised. (6) Add the double-click test: two clicks, exactly one schedule-edit-modal, Cancel once, table visible. (7) Rename only the three page-model methods that widened to `number | Locator`; leave the six that still take an index alone. Add editSchedule(row). Leave getByRole('menu') unscoped, matching the seven other unscoped uses. qa_script: Boot: yarn start, open http://localhost:3001, choose "Don't use a server" then "View demo".

validated_work_order.debate_summary:
The previous plan (v3) was rejected with one numbered objection, and it is correct on the source. I verified it line by line before replanning rather than defending the old text.

The objection: the plan told the implementer to assert the trigger's 'once' description BEFORE clicking Apply, in `understanding` step 3 and `files[4].change` (a), and that assertion cannot pass. The trigger renders the `value` prop (RecurringSchedulePicker.tsx:632, memoised on [locale, value, dateFormat]); `value` is fields.date (ScheduleEditForm.tsx:261) and reaches the picker's onChange from exactly one place, onSave (:607-609), wired to Apply at :579. Everything before Apply is local to the tooltip — the change-field reducer, the re-seed effect that reads the same unchanged currentConfig, and the preview effect that only sets previewDates. So while the popover is open the trigger renders the seeded endMode 'never' and reads 'Every month on the 4th', with no ', once'. The negative half would have passed vacuously while the positive half failed.

What I changed, exactly where the reviewer asked: in `understanding` step 3a and `files[4].change` (a), the 'once' assertion now sits AFTER Apply, with the reason stated inline — the trigger renders the `value` prop and Apply is the picker's only write-back. I also took the reviewer's optional suggestion and added the pre-Apply state as its own case: while the popover is open the trigger still reads 'Every month on the 4th' with no ', once'. That turns the write-back boundary into something the test pins at both ends rather than a claim the plan merely made. tests[0].cases[1] and [2] are split the same way, and qa_script reads the button at both moments (steps 5 and 7).

The reviewer also asked me to re-read the plan for any other place the pre/post-Apply split had drifted, and to make `debate_summary` match what `files[]` actually says. I re-checked every mention of the trigger's text: AC-1's how_to_verify was already correct (it reads the button after Apply), qa_script steps 5-6 were already correct, and `files[1].why` describes the string without claiming a moment. The two wrong places were the only two, and both are fixed above. This `debate_summary` now describes the file as it is written, not as it was intended.

One further change, made on my own judgement and disclosed here rather than buried. The previous plan carried four verify:"test" criteria, two of which (its old AC-2 and AC-4) were properties of a diff — "read schedules.test.ts and confirm these identifiers are gone" — with no verifier in any stage, and two more whose only proof was a Playwright run that no CI job performs. An earlier review of this same ticket rejected exactly that shape and told the planner to carry those requirements as notes on the files[] descriptions instead. The v3 plan did not do so.
